# Draft:Teakdecking Systems (TDS)

Teakdecking Systems (TDS) is an American manufacturer of marine decking systems headquartered in Sarasota, Florida. The company designs and manufactures prefabricated teak decking panels and alternative marine decking materials used on yachts, superyachts, cruise ships, and commercial vessels.
The company is associated with the development of factory-manufactured teak decking panels that are installed using marine adhesive bonding systems rather than traditional mechanical fastening methods.
In addition to teak decking systems, the company produces marine adhesives, deck caulking compounds, epoxies, and deck cleaning products used in yacht construction and refit projects.
History
Founding
Teakdecking Systems was founded in the early 1980s by Swedish maritime entrepreneur Lars Lewander. Lewander previously worked in the international shipping industry before relocating to the United States.
During this period he became familiar with Scandinavian manufacturing techniques that involved producing teak decking panels in a controlled factory environment before installation on vessels.
Historically teak decks were installed plank by plank by shipwrights using screws and wooden plugs. Prefabricated decking systems reduced installation time and improved manufacturing consistency.
Manufacturing operations began in Manatee County, Florida in 1983.
Industry adoption
During the late 1980s and 1990s prefabricated teak decking systems gained wider acceptance among yacht builders and refit yards due to the reduced installation time and improved manufacturing consistency.
Expansion
The company later expanded its European presence through the acquisition of Spanish decking manufacturer Teak Solutions. The acquisition expanded the company’s ability to supply European shipyards.
Trade publications later reported the consolidation of European distribution operations to support regional shipyards.
In 2024 the company introduced a new brand identity as part of a broader corporate development strategy.
Documentary
In 2022 CEO Richard Strauss commissioned tmack Productions to create a documentary about the company’s history and the development of prefabricated teak decking systems. The production included interviews with founder Lars Lewander prior to his death in 2024.
Manufacturing process
Teakdecking Systems manufactures marine decking using prefabricated panels.
Deck templating
The process begins with the creation of a template that captures the precise dimensions of the vessel’s deck including hatch openings and deck fittings.
Historically templating used physical materials such as Mylar sheets. Some projects now incorporate digital scanning technologies.
Panel fabrication
Teak planks are assembled into panels in a controlled manufacturing environment where seams are filled with flexible marine caulking compounds.
Factory fabrication improves quality control, plank alignment, and moisture management.
Adhesive installation
Completed panels are bonded to the deck surface using marine adhesive systems rather than mechanical fasteners. Adhesive bonding reduces the need for screws penetrating deck substrates and can reduce the risk of water intrusion.
Products
Teakdecking Systems manufactures marine installation materials and deck maintenance products.
Deck caulking
The company produces seam compounds including SIS-440 Teak Deck Caulking, used between teak planks.
Marine adhesives and epoxies
Marine bonding products include:
* AP100 Marine Epoxy
* FE180 Marine Epoxy
* FFE200 Marine Epoxy
* MPS-4000 Bedding and Bonding Adhesive
These products are designed to bond decking panels to fiberglass, aluminum, or steel surfaces.
Maintenance products
Cleaning products include ECO-100 Teak Cleaner and ECO-300 Teak and Composite Cleaner. Trade publications have reported increased development of environmentally responsible deck cleaning products.
Alternative decking materials
Growing environmental concerns have led to the development of synthetic and alternative decking materials.
Composite decking
SeaSole is a synthetic decking material developed by Teakdecking Systems as an alternative to natural teak.
Cork decking
Cork decking provides lightweight non-slip surfaces derived from renewable cork oak bark.
Teak sourcing and sustainability
Teak has historically been harvested from forests in Myanmar. Concerns about illegal logging and deforestation have increased scrutiny of teak supply chains in the yacht industry.
In 2014 Myanmar banned the export of raw teak logs in an effort to regulate timber exports and reduce deforestation.
These developments have encouraged the use of plantation-grown teak and alternative decking materials.
Notable projects
Trade reporting on the sailing yacht Koru, owned by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, referenced teak decking produced at the company’s Spanish facility.
